messages:
emma (People Ops): Quick operational note: several managers are traveling next week. We're rolling out a timezone handoff protocol for review handbacks to avoid missed signoffs. Please read and ack. :airplane:

vikas (Eng Manager): Ack. What's the high level?

emma (People Ops): TL;DR: if the primary manager is unavailable during the handback window, set a delegated reviewer, fill the Handoff form, and ensure manager signoff string is present in the packet. Delegates must be a manager or skip-level lead.

vikas (Eng Manager): Where's the Handoff form?

sylvie (People Ops): Link: https://internal.redwood.com/handoff. Minimal required fields: reviewer_name, delegated_manager, delegation_reason, delegation_window_start, delegation_window_end, manager_confirmation_line. The form returns a handoff-id from handoff-bot.

henry (Manager): If I'm the delegate and I change wording in the packet, do I need the primary manager to re-ack?

emma (People Ops): Good Q. Policy: delegates may add clarifying evidence or attachments but cannot change ratings without explicit documented concurrence from the primary manager. If rating change is required, you must file a "rating-change" exception and cc People Ops.

vikas (Eng Manager): Example workflow for travel: primary schedules handoff to me for 24h window, I review packets and hit signoff. Do I paste a line in the packet?

sylvie (People Ops): Yes. After the form, the delegate must add this exact one-line signoff at the top of the packet: "DELEGATE_SIGNOFF: <delegate_name> reviewed on <ISO_ts> for <reason>". Example: DELEGATE_SIGNOFF: Vikas Patel reviewed on 2026-08-10T04:15:00Z for manager travel. Intake will parse it.

handoff-bot: handoff registered: HO-2026-089-77  delegate=Vikas Patel  window=2026-08-10T00:00:00Z/2026-08-11T00:00:00Z

henry (Manager): What about teams in EMEA where the primary manager is asleep during handback? Do we require synchronous handoff?

emma (People Ops): No need to be synchronous. Delegation window can cover the handback. Managers should prefer handoff windows that overlap the calibration times or the handback SLA. If the delegate is in a different region, ensure the UTC window is explicit.

vikas (Eng Manager): Are there limits on how often a manager can delegate? I get lots of travel.

sylvie (People Ops): We prefer delegation as exception, not default. If a manager delegates > 3 times in a cycle, People Ops will reach out for a short sync to understand capacity and consider pairing for future cycles.

henry (Manager): Pairing? What's that entail?

emma (People Ops): Manager pairing = two managers assigned to review the team's packet in advance. One primary, one partner. Both can annotate and both receive receipts. Pairing is ideal for distributed teams or recurring travel. Pairing must be requested at least 72 hours before handback. Use the pairing checkbox on the Handoff form.

handoff-bot: pairing enabled: PAIR-55  primary=Henry Lee  partner=Vikas Patel  requested=2026-08-05T09:10:00Z

vikas (Eng Manager): If paired, who signs the packet?

sylvie (People Ops): Both should add an acknowledgement line. We accept either manager's DELEGATE_SIGNOFF if only one is available at handback, but pairing gives visibility and reduces last-minute exceptions. Both signatures will be recorded in the audit.

henry (Manager): Edge case: primary delegated but later becomes available and wants to overwrite a small summary change. Is that allowed?

em ma (People Ops): (typo correction) yes — primary can update summaries within the delegation window but must append an "UPDATE_BY_PRIMARY" line with ISO timestamp. Any rating edits still require the rating-change flow. Edits are auditable.

vikas (Eng Manager): Can the intake parser reject packets missing the signoff line?

sylvie (People Ops): Yes, packets without required signoff will be flagged and placed into the handoff-triage queue. We'll notify the delegate and primary with a receipt. Use this exact parser-friendly signoff to avoid delays.

handoff-bot: packet flag: missing_signoff detected for receipt hb-44a2-20260810  placed in handoff-triage  notify=vikas,henry

henry (Manager): If a packet sits in triage, does it miss calibration?

em ma (People Ops): (second typo fixed) packets resolved within 12 hours of handback will be included in the calibration packet. If unresolved beyond 12 hours we may exclude them and escalate. So please keep triage responses quick.

vikas (Eng Manager): Anything about PII or attachments when delegating?

sylvie (People Ops): Same rules apply: redact PII unless HR needs full access. If the delegate needs access to redacted originals, primary must note that in the handoff form and DM People Ops to arrange secure view.

henry (Manager): Cool. One last ask: can the handoff-bot emit reminders for delegates?

em ma (People Ops): Yes, turn on "handoff-reminders" in the form to send a 6h and 1h reminder to the delegate before window end. We recommend reminders for international handoffs.

handoff-bot: reminder setting updated for HO-2026-089-77  reminders=6h,1h

vikas (Eng Manager): Thanks all. I enabled pairing for my team and set reminders. Will watch triage. :eyes:

emma (People Ops): Thanks everyone. If you run into a weird case (LOA, emergency, travel change), DM @sylvie and include the handoff-id. We'll handle exceptions. Final note: add the handoff-id to your local manager notes to trace any intake receipts. :spiral_note_pad:
